1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..strategy: The sharp main move: the knight eyes d6 and c7, and with the queen behind it Nd6+ is a real threat that would win the bishop pair. Black has to deal with it at once, and the incursion makes d6 the focus of the whole middlegame.

Trades the d4 knight for the one on c6 to gain a tempo: if Black recaptures with the b-pawn, e5 hits the f6 knight and drives it back. White gets space and the initiative at the price of releasing the central tension; the e5 pawn needs care and the lines are double-edged.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..name: Sicilian Defence: Four Knights Variation, Exchange Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..background: This option has become more popular over time, but it remains less popular than 6.Ndb5.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..strategy: Plugs the d6 hole with a pawn and prepares ...e5, heading for a structure with a backward d6 pawn and a weak d5 square. Black accepts that lasting weakness in return for active pieces, central space and play against the knight on b5.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..name: Sicilian Defence: Four Knights Variation, Sveshnikov Transfer

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..strategy: Pins the c3 knight against the king, so e4 is effectively undefended and ...Nxe4 is threatened. White has to react, and the bishop may take on c3, which gives up the bishop pair for easy development and central play.

Brings the bishop to an active diagonal where it covers d6 and eyes f2. But White can still invade on the dark squares around c7 and d6, and the main line runs through a series of exchanges that can end in a drawish endgame.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6 5..name: Sicilian Defence: Four Knights Variation, Cobra Variation
